> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/src/kernel/manifest.zod.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `safeParse (5 routes)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **147** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 038d4c958837fb42e71842c18f062f37bd866811` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `85f41ef4183bc50018fb8ed525b5e5f2c7f4d516` — the merge of head `58984f5c5baf2eb298c8346f1a05ddf8e8d885a6` into base `038d4c958837fb42e71842c18f062f37bd866811`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 85f41ef4183bc50018fb8ed525b5e5f2c7f4d516 && git checkout 85f41ef4183bc50018fb8ed525b5e5f2c7f4d516
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 038d4c958837fb42e71842c18f062f37bd866811 58984f5c5baf2eb298c8346f1a05ddf8e8d885a6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 038d4c958837fb42e71842c18f062f37bd866811 && git merge --no-ff 58984f5c5baf2eb298c8346f1a05ddf8e8d885a6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 038d4c958837fb42e71842c18f062f37bd866811
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 038d4c958837fb42e71842c18f062f37bd866811` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `58984f5c5baf2eb298c8346f1a05ddf8e8d885a6`
Local-runs: none

Rendered 2026-10-12T21:06Z by the isolated at-tier reviewer subagent of `domain:spec` seat 1 (seat post #6017, account `os-warren`) on PR #23075 (`Part of #15213`, the `_lock` strip). Read-only: the PR body, its 14-file list and the net diff against `main` (804 changed lines, read against the merge base the PR body's affected-closure measurement names), card #15213's body and all 46 comments, ruling `6119681934` on #22971 and its close `6119699999`, and the check-runs on this head. Nothing built, run or re-run; the fork PR test is moot (head repo is the base repo). The head sha was confirmed from the REST read of the PR before anything else was read.

### ① Derived judgments

**The published surface this diff implies, judged line by line against the diff:**

1. **`@objectstack/spec` — `ImportUnmanagedPackageResponseSchema` gains the required field `strippedLocks`** (`packages/spec/src/api/package-lifecycle.zod.ts`): an array of `{ type, name, lock, reason? }`, `lock` taken as `MetadataLockSchema.exclude(['none'])` from the one lock declaration in `kernel/metadata-protection.zod.ts`, never restated. **Right.** This is the ruling's "the import result names each stripped lock together with the vendor's reason", declared exactly once; the only non-test producer on `main` is `importUnmanagedPackage` (`protocol.ts`), and at this head it states the field. The three generated artifacts moved with it and nothing else: `authorable-surface/api.json` (+1 key), `content/docs/references/api/package-lifecycle.mdx` (the field and its nested shape), the strictness ledger count 437 → 438. No export was added or removed in spec, so no `api-surface` shard moves. A required field on a `z.input` response type is a widening for its producer; no code in the repo parses another runtime's answer with this schema, and the CLI reads the field through `Array.isArray` so a runtime that predates it prints nothing. `(widening)` is the right arm.
2. **`packages/spec/src/kernel/manifest.zod.ts` — the `INSTALL_MODES` TSDoc only.** No shape moves. **Right.**
3. **`@objectstack/metadata-protocol` — the import's behaviour:** every planned item is written without `_lock`, `_lockReason`, `_lockSource`, `_lockDocsUrl` and, on a type whose schema declares the key, without its `protection` block; the plan carries `strippedLocks` in write order and the verb returns it. **Right.** The published surface of the package does not move: `src/index.ts` at this head exports neither `stripUnmanagedImportLock`, `overlaySchemaDeclaredKey`, `UnmanagedImportStrippedLock` nor `DeclaredValueJudge` (it names only `unmanagedInstallPostureRefusal` from the pure module and a closed list from `protocol.ts`), and `package.json`'s `exports` map has the single `.` entry. The verb's return type is spec's, so the one published change is item 1. The dev's acceptance note that the two new exports are module-level for the tests only is confirmed on the head.
4. **Refusals of the unmanaged import — unchanged.** Confirmed in the head's `package-unmanaged-install.ts`: the key dispositions (`UNMANAGED_INSTALL_KEY_DISPOSITIONS`) are judged on the manifest's collection keys before `enumerateItems`, and the strip runs on the enumerated items after the sort; `stripUnmanagedImportLock` hands the body back untouched when any envelope key fails its own declaration (`MetadataProtectionFields`) or the block fails the type's own `protection` schema, and it leaves a `protection` block on a type whose schema declares none, so the save door refuses those exactly as on `main` (`422 INVALID_METADATA`, rolled back; pinned at the unit level for `_lock: 'locked'` and for a `page` carrying the block, and the every-type ablation turned the `page` pin red). Nothing previously refused is accepted and nothing previously accepted is refused. **Right.** The one corner the dev flagged — envelope keys plus a block on a non-declaring type — ends in the door's refusal and a rollback, so no answer and no `strippedLocks` is ever returned for that body.
5. **The entry for an item carrying both spellings is the lock a managed install binds.** Confirmed against `packages/spec/src/shared/protection.zod.ts`: `applyProtection` writes the block's `lock` and `reason` over `_lock` / `_lockReason` when the block states them, so the strip's scratch-copy translation reports one entry with the block's values and `'none'` reports nothing. The dogfood lock control measures the same on a real managed install. **Right** — the report is the managed binding, not a second rule.
6. **Seat decision 1 (`6128999134`): strip the `protection` block on declaring types and report it — judged WITHIN ruling A's text, not beyond it.** Ruling A's operative sentences are "the unmanaged import strips every lock from each copied item, and the import result names each stripped lock together with the vendor's reason" and "Visible, not silent". Its bullet names `_lock` / `_lockReason` / `_lockSource` on a stated premise — "whether the lock was authored per item or resolved from `metadataDefaults.lock` by the loader (both arrive as the same L3 shape)" — that is, the ruling meant to reach every lock a package ships and believed all of them arrive as the L3 envelope. That premise is measured false on both halves (no schema declares `metadataDefaults`; the `protection` block arrives untranslated). ADR-0010 Phase 4.3 defines `protection` as the public author surface that "translates into the private `_lock` envelope at load time" — the same lock in its authored spelling, and the spelling the guidance tells authors to write. Under the ruling's own rationale ("a lock whose source is the package has nothing to stand on once the package is no longer the authority"), the block is a package lock; keeping it inert on the copy would be the silent loss the ruling forbids and a declared-but-unenforced block in the row (Prime Directive #10); stripping it on every type would move a refusal, which the ruling costs no gate for. Stripping it only where the type's own schema declares it, reported in the ruling's entry shape, with no new field, no new gate and no refusal moved, is the ruling applied to the spelling its premise mis-described. It is not a new product decision and needs no decision-box entry; the seat recorded the maintainer's veto window on it, which is the right form.
7. **Seat decision 2 (`6128999134`): strip `_lockDocsUrl` with the other three keys, no new report field — judged WITHIN ruling A's text.** It is the fourth member of the one declared envelope (`MetadataProtectionFields` in spec; `LOCK_FAMILY_KEYS` in `item-lock.ts`); `applyProtection` writes it as part of the same translation; once `_lock` is gone it is served nowhere and binds nothing, so leaving it would leave an orphan lock-family key in the row. "Strips every lock" takes the lock's whole envelope. The option that would have gone beyond — a `docsUrl` field on each entry — was not taken.
8. **The install door** (`@objectstack/cloud-connection`) relays `result.strippedLocks` as the verb states it, and the managed branch's answer carries no such key (pinned in dogfood). **Right.** The door's unmanaged answer has no spec declaration of its own on `main` (a pre-existing fact of S2's landing, not moved here), so there is no second declaration owed.
9. **The CLI** prints each entry as `TYPE.NAME: LOCK — REASON`, the dash and reason absent when the package gave none, and prints no lock line for an empty list or an answer without one. **Right** — this is the ruling's own spelling, rendered from the structured field, which is the correct form for a machine-read answer.
10. **The changeset** supersedes the two `_lock` sentences of the pending `15213-install-modes` entry by statement rather than by editing it; that entry is still pending on `origin/main` and says the copy keeps an authored `_lock`. **Right** — both ship in one release, so no published version ever carried the kept-lock behaviour; nothing is removed or narrowed, and `check:adr-0087-registration` owes no marker.
11. **Governed surfaces:** none of the 14 paths hits a `GOVERNED_SURFACES` row; `docs/audits/**` is not one. The review is owed on the `Clause-②: yes` and `packages/spec/src/**` faces, which this record serves; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is green on the head.

**Check-runs on this head (the gate verdicts):** 48 check runs, 41 `success`, 7 `skipped`, 0 `failure`. The seven required contexts: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` (and its six shards), `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Build Core` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` succeeded; `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` was skipped by its own paths filter, as were the dogfood matrix shards, `Console Pin Gate`, `Dogfood Verify CLI` and the opt-in packed-tarball smoke. The PR reads `mergeable: true`, `mergeable_state: clean`, draft, auto-merge not armed, no review submitted.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/spec`: **minor** — one new required field on a published response declaration; no export added or removed. Matches the changeset.
- `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`: **minor** — the verb's answer gains the field and the copy no longer carries a lock; the package index publishes nothing new. Matches.
- `@objectstack/cloud-connection`: **minor** — the unmanaged answer gains the field. Matches.
- `@objectstack/cli`: **minor** — new output lines. Matches.
- The declaration agrees across the claim (`6126585884`), the PR body and the changeset: `Clause-②: yes (widening: the new response field strippedLocks on ImportUnmanagedPackageResponseSchema, relayed on the install-local answer for installMode unmanaged)`. `yes` takes at least `minor` — held; the `(widening)` arm is the right one and owes no ADR-0087 disposition marker. `Check Changeset` and `Lint & Repo Gates` are green on the head. The superseded sentences live only in the pending `15213-install-modes` entry, so nothing released is narrowed and no migration text is owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Round 1 report `6128963245`, deviations:**
1. A2 falsified, `metadataDefaults` pinned as refused `422 UNMANAGED_INSTALL_UNCOPYABLE` instead of stripped — **answered, right**: no schema declares the key, the pin is in the diff and reddens the day the key is declared and classified.
2. `protection` not stripped in round 1 — **superseded** by seat decision 1, implemented at this head (① item 6).
3. `_lockDocsUrl` left in round 1 — **superseded** by seat decision 2, implemented at this head (① item 7).
4. `origin/main` merged once mid-stage, no conflicts — **answered**: that merge is the merge base this record's diff was read against.
5. The dogfood managed-control red on base was a fixture bug in reading the `GET /meta` envelope, corrected in the PR — **answered**: a fixture correction inside this diff; the head's fixture reads `data ?? body`.
6. Model-free commit trailers — **answered**: the form AGENTS.md requires.
7. Session-URL footer on the PR body — **answered**: the form AGENTS.md requires; the body carries exactly one footer.

**Round 1 open questions** (both): decided by the seat in `6128999134` and built in round 2; judged in ① items 6 and 7 as within the ruling.

**Round 1 out-of-scope finding** (class c, the `protection` block stored and never bound on an environment item): **answered** — a save-door defect outside this diff, which the PR correctly does not fix; the ACCEPT `6132465308` records it filed as #23096. That issue was not read here (outside this record's input set).

**Round 2 report `6132411048`, deviations:**
1. PR body not edited by the dev, the replacement handed to the seat — **answered**: the PR body read here is that replacement, one footer.
2. `@objectstack/cli`'s `integration` project left to CI — **answered**: `Test Core` 1–6 are green on the head.
3. Lock-holder load on the shared verify lock — **answered**: a process note with no contract bearing.
4. The first `check:generated --fix` timed out on the lock; the one stale artifact was regenerated with `gen:docs` and the rerun read all 14 current — **answered**: the `TypeScript Type Check` job, which runs the spec `check:*` gates, is green on the head.
5. Envelope keys plus a `protection` block on a non-declaring type: envelope stripped, block left, door refuses `422` — **answered, right**: judged in ① item 4; nothing new is accepted and no answer is returned for that body.
6. Model-free commit trailers — **answered**, as above.

**Round 2 open questions:** none.

**Round 2 out-of-scope findings:**
1. The Studio save door accepts, stores, serves and never binds a hand-authored `protection` block on an environment item (class c; the Seam is `ViewSchema.protection` and siblings to `saveMetaItem` / `item-lock.ts`) — **answered**: outside this diff; carried by #23096 per the ACCEPT; this PR leaves it alone and, for declaring types, no longer writes such a block itself.
2. A managed dataset's `GET /meta/dataset/:name` answers without the top-level lock envelope that `GET /meta/dashboard/:name` answers (uninvestigated) — **answered**: an observation on the read path, which this diff does not touch, so it bears on no contract here. One records gap for the seat: the ACCEPT says "Acceptance notes, carrier none", but the PR body's acceptance notes do not carry it — it lives only in the report and the ACCEPT. Under Prime Directive #10 the seat owes it a carrier: a line in the PR body's acceptance notes, or an issue once it reproduces. Not verdict-bearing.
3. S3 (the authoring page) states that an unmanaged copy keeps no lock in either spelling and that the install lists each lock it drops — **answered**: matches the seat's carry; S3 and S4 stay on the card, and the PR says `Part of #15213` with no closing keyword.

No flag is escalated: neither seat decision goes beyond ruling A, no refusal moved, and the one defect found is carried by its own issue.
